items.title: 68163_Tom Whaley oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] You know, in observing Duke's band... perhaps in later years, the clarinet player that's down in the West Indies now. >> [INTERVIEWEE] Jimmy Hamilton.

ctx.x: You know, in observing Duke's band, the guys that always seemed to me most reliable was like Harry Carney, you know, when they took intermission and the band came back out after intermission you could always depend on Carney to be back on time and you could always depend on perhaps in later years, the clarinet player that's down in the West Indies now.

Jimmy Hamilton and I think that's -- I remember once seeing that band, and after intermission Duke would play something, he made this little call -------- he made that little call to call off the men back and the guys were out socializing with the chicks and talking to the customers, Duke would be the only one on the bandstand and pretty soon you see Carney come up and he would start something like Mood Indigo where he only needed three or four of them to get it started.
